clue.text: Gathered in a gym, looking embarrassed about it?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the embarrassed word wraps the gym letters

parts.note: someone looking embarrassed has gone red
PE, physical education, is the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: Someone in a gym, blushing about what they have taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' is the past tense of harvesting, not collecting a crowd; PE (physical education) is the school gym lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have harvested a crop is to have gathered it in.

clue.text: Heather being entertained by Americans

indicators.note: something entertained by a word is held as a guest inside it, so the letters sit within Americans

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather is the guest of some Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: erica is the genus name for heather.

clue.text: 'Downtown' performer pleasant, not one for sulkiness

parts.note: Petula Clark sang the 1960s hit Downtown

indicators.note: not one asks for the letter I, the Roman one, to be left out

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A singer known for Downtown is pleasant, not a sulker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' takes I out of NICE, leaving NCE. Petula Clark was a British pop singer whose biggest hit was Downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: petulance is peevish bad temper, much like sulkiness.

clue.text: Stop revolutionary rocker grabbing girl

indicators.note: grabbing means holding something inside, so the girl goes within
revolutionary means turned round, so the rocker's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s rocker
sis, short for sister, is a girl

explanation.surface: A call to stop a rebellious rock musician seizing a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted (Teddy boy) was a 1950s British youth who loved rock and roll; 'revolutionary' turns his name round to DET before the girl goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cease or refrain from an action is to stop.

clue.text: Playful nonsense outside station

indicators.note: outside means the nonsense word goes round the station word

parts.note: pish is an exclamation dismissing something as nonsense
one's station in life is one's rank

explanation.surface: Light-hearted rubbish heard around a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests trains, but it means social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: given to practical jokes, so mischievously playful.

clue.text: In which every picture tells a story?

definitions.text: In which every picture tells a story?

parts.words: In which every picture tells a story?
parts.note: the saying that every picture tells a story describes news reporting done through photographs

explanation.surface: A musing on the old saying that every picture tells a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is taken literally: a branch of reporting where the images carry the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: news reporting by camera, where pictures are the story.

clue.text: Story enacted fantastically, full of love

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so love goes within
fantastically signals the letters of enacted are wildly rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tale acted out in a fantastical way, brimming with romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges ENACTED to ANECDTE, and 'full of' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short amusing tale from real life is a story.

clue.text: Sort of informal relations joined by a daughter turning up

parts.note: one's relations are one's kin

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Family members joined by a daughter who arrives, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses A D to DA. 'informal' marks the definition as slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a casual spoken form of kind of, meaning somewhat or sort of.

clue.text: Supporters of Elizabeth II, so to speak

definitions.meaning: people who back a motion formally in a meeting

definitions.text: of Elizabeth II, so to speak
definitions.meaning: people belonging to the Second, a whimsical coinage from Elizabeth the Second

explanation.surface: Royalists who backed the late Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up word: those of the Second, hence 'so to speak'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting jargon: those who back a proposal after it is moved are its supporters.

clue.text: Gem of a baby

parts.note: each month of birth has its own precious stone, so a baby has a gem linked to it

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely child, a real gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem of a baby' sounds like doting praise; read literally it is the jewel tied to a baby's month of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition: a precious stone assigned to each calendar month of birth.

clue.text: Saintly December traveller briefly in prison

definitions.meaning: Saint Nicholas, who travels at Christmas, is known by a short form of his name
British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: Santa Claus finds himself locked up for a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the short form of Nicholas. In British slang 'the nick' is a police station or jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: being locked up in the nick means being in jail.

clue.text: Name is given to satellite of Jupiter

parts.note: to name someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A name is assigned to one of Jupiter's moons.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy: one of the large Galilean moons orbiting Jupiter.

clue.text: Hard rain sometimes will be too much for such

definitions.text: Hard rain sometimes will be too much for such

indicators.note: too much for suggests overflowing something; here the answer is held, overflowing, within the opening three words

explanation.surface: A warning that a downpour can overwhelm the gutters.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'Hard rain sometimes', and the whole clue also describes it: a deluge can overwhelm channels built for runoff.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: channels and pipes carrying away rainwater can flood in a deluge.

clue.text: Study accommodating a person who sometimes writes sermon?

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the study holds the letter inside

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A study with room for a preacher writing a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts A inside DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a senior cathedral cleric who will at times compose and preach sermons.

clue.text: Page is one trained for secret work

indicators.note: trained hints the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A young page has been schooled for undercover duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges the letters of PAGE IS ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: spying is covert intelligence work.

clue.text: Got old boy schooled, having missed one of three basic subjects?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: having missed means leaving out, so one letter drops from the schooled word

parts.note: schooled means trained
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so one is R

explanation.surface: A former pupil got his education but skipped a core subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having missed' drops R from TRAINED. The three Rs are the basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have acquired or gained something is to have got it.

clue.text: Wriggling inside mum, as many a baby will be

definitions.text: as many a baby will be

indicators.note: wriggling suggests the letters squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: An unborn baby wriggling in its mother's womb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggling' rearranges INSIDE MUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: most infants get vaccinated, made protected against disease.

clue.text: Examiner of idiots, upset no end

parts.note: fools are asses

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is cut off the upset word

parts.note: sore means upset or aggrieved

explanation.surface: An examiner of fools gets endlessly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops E from SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who evaluates or judges, such as for tax or exams.

clue.text: A very quiet repose, right for one avoiding conflict

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
repose means ease or rest

explanation.surface: Calm rest is right for someone who shuns arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) is the music marking for very soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a placater who gives in to keep the peace dodges conflict.

clue.text: Maiden given River, a strong perfume

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A young woman named after a river wears heavy scent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Usk is a river in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pungent animal-derived scent used in perfumery.

clue.text: Sector abroad providing bodyguard

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A foreign region supplying protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an armed guard accompanying someone for protection.

clue.text: Twins maybe left in car

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: Twin children abandoned in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside COUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: twins make a pair, two of a kind.

clue.text: Country's number two making little money

definitions.meaning: Mike ... was US Vice-President, the nation's second in command
small coins in British currency, pennies

explanation.surface: A deputy leader earning very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence was Vice-President of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: British coinage: pennies are small sums of money.

clue.text: A busy type getting sent inside — has one escaped?

indicators.note: inside means the sent letters go within the busy creature

parts.note: a bee is the proverbial busy creature

explanation.surface: A busy worker gets jailed, prompting a question about a breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent inside' reads as being jailed, which feeds the escape question.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person missing from where they should be, as if escaped.

clue.text: Be unfair to a woman maybe in want of a roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, here lacking

parts.note: being sexist is being unfair because of gender

explanation.surface: Being unjust to a homeless woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in want of a roof' removes the top letter, S, from SEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to live or have being is simply to be.

clue.text: Enthusiast embraces upper-class character of godlike nature

indicators.note: embraces means hugging something inside, so the posh letter goes within

parts.note: an enthusiast is a fan

explanation.surface: A fan clutches a posh figure with a divine air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts U inside FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: a rural Roman deity, half man and half goat, a minor god.

clue.text: Finery for Jack the Lad?

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, and a lad might be dressed up in naval-style clothes

explanation.surface: Flashy clothes for a cocky young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack the Lad' is British slang for a brash young man, but jack is also a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boy's naval-style outfit, worn as Sunday best.

clue.text: Short sad poem penned in vehicle gives urgent message

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the poem sits inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the poem loses its last letter

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem

explanation.surface: A brief lament written on a bus sends an urgent note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the poem, and 'penned in' places what remains inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: History: a wired message, once the fastest way to send urgent news.

clue.text: Retro function held in gallery until now

indicators.note: held in means placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the function word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: A vintage-themed party at an art gallery, up to the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' turns DO to OD and 'held in' places it in TATE, the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: so far, up to the present moment.
